Theorem
[Regularity on a ball]1. ch4:4.13,ch4:4.31,ch4:4.32\group ch04-poisson-newtonian-potential Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0079 Let $B$ be a ball. If $u\in C^2(B)\cap C^0(\overline B)$, $f\in C^\alpha (\overline B)$, $\Delta u=f$, and $u=0$ on $\partial B$, then $u\in C^{2,\alpha }(\overline B)$.
Proof

\sketch Translate a boundary point to the origin. Inversion and the Kelvin transform

\begin{equation} \tag {4.31} v(x)=|x|^{2-n}u(x/|x|^2) \end{equation}

map the ball locally to a half-space and satisfy

\begin{equation} \tag {4.32} \Delta v(x^*)=|x^*|^{-n-2}(\Delta u)(x). \end{equation}

Apply Theorem 23 at each boundary point and the interior estimate away from the boundary.

□
